The Court Made The Following:
 Order

Accused Nos.1 to 5 are before this Court under Section 482 of Cr.P.C with a prayer to quash the entire NC: 2024:KHC-K:3751 proceedings in Crime No.50/2024 registered by the Afzalpur Police Station, Kalaburagi for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 354, 504 and 506 read with Section 149 of Cr.P.C based on the information received from respondent No.2 herein on 22.03.2024.
2.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties.

3. FIR in Crime No.50/2024 was registered by the Afzalpur Police Station, Kalaburagi against petitioners herein for the aforesaid offences on the basis of the first information submitted by respondent No.2 herein who is the wife of first petitioner.
Petitioner No.2 is the elder sister of petitioner No.1 and petitioner Nos.3 to 5 are the children of petitioner No.2.
Being aggrieved by the registration of FIR in Crime No.50/2024 lodged against petitioners, they are before this Court.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners having reiterated the grounds urged in the petition submits that undisputedly respondent No.2 has left the company of petitioner No.1 and residing in her parents' house.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:3751 Petitioner No.1 has been taking care of the four minor children.
In respect of the alleged incident dated 11.03.2023 belatedly after a period of more than one year, FIR has been registered.
He submits that only to harass and coerce the petitioners a false complaint has been made against them by respondent No.2.
He submits that absolutely there is no material as against petitioner Nos.3 to 5 and inspite of the same they have been arrayed as accused in the FIR.

Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
5.
Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1/State and learned counsel for respondent No.2 have opposed the petition.

They submit that respondent No.2 was in a fond hope that she would be taken back to the matrimonial house and therefore even though the alleged incident had taken place on 11.03.2203, she had approached the police belatedly on 22.03.2024.
They submit that there are specific allegations as against accused Nos.1 and 2 and therefore investigation NC: 2024:KHC-K:3751 in the case is necessary.
Accordingly, they pray to dismiss the petition.

6. From the perusal of the averments made in the first information dated 22.03.2024 which has resulted in registration of FIR in Crime No.50/2024 against the petitioners, it is seen that the marriage of respondent No.2 was solemnized with petitioner No.1/accused No.1 in the year 2010 and from the said wedlock the couple have four children.
As per the allegations made in the first information, initially the accused No.1 was looking after his wife properly and thereafter he was suspecting her character and used to abuse and assault her.
It is in this background, respondent No.2 had left the company of her husband and had taken shelter in her parents' house for the last two years.

It is alleged in the first information that on 11.03.2023 at about 11.00 a.m. petitioner Hanamant And Ors vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5018378/
3 Nos.1 and 2 came to the house of first informant's parents and started abusing her.

sentences.text:
When her mother tried to intervene, accused No.1 allegedly caught hold of her hair and pulled her to NC:
2024:KHC-K:3751 the road and kicked her on her stomach, accused No.2 allegedly instigated accused No.1.
The neighbourers of the first informant intervened and thereafter accused Nos.1 and 2 allegedly left the spot after criminally intimidating the first informant and her family members.

7. Though the alleged incident had taken place on 11.03.2023 the first informant has belatedly approached the police on 22.03.2024 and submitted a typed first information, based on which the impugned criminal proceeding has been registered.
No satisfactory reason has been given by the first informant explaining the inordinate delay of more than one year in approaching the police.

In addition to the same, though accused No.3 to 5/petitioner Nos.3 to 5 were not at all present at the spot on the alleged date of incident that had taken place on 11.03.2023, they have been arrayed as accused in the impugned proceedings by making omnibus allegation as against them.
According to the first informant, she had left the company of her husband about two years prior to she approaching the police.
Therefore, it becomes highly doubtful that on 11.03.2023, accused Nos.1 and 2 came to her parents house and had committed the alleged offence.
In addition to the same, the material on record would go to show that respondent No.2 had left her four minor children in the custody of her husband and had taken shelter in her parents' house.
In the background of conduct of respondent No.2, if the allegations made in the first information are analyzed, the allegations made in the first information becomes highly doubtful.
In addition to the aforesaid aspects of the matter, the first informant had approached the police after delay of more than one year from the alleged date of incident.
9. Under the circumstances, I am of the opinion that the registration and continuation of the criminal proceedings as against the petitioners herein is abuse of process of law.
Therefore, for the purpose of securing ends NC: 2024:KHC-K:3751 of justice, it is just and necessary to quash the same.
Accordingly, the following :
ORDER The criminal petition is allowed.

The further proceedings in Crime No.50/2024 registered by Afzalpur Police Station, Kalaburagi for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 354, 504 and 506 read with Section 149 of Cr.P.C pending before the Court of Civil Judge (Jr.Dn.) and JMFC, Afzalpur, stands quashed.
